2026-12-07.verse: If in my name you ask me for anything, I will do it.
theo: Paul's goal for the Church is maturity: “until all of us come to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to maturity, to the measure of the full stature of Christ.” No longer “children, tossed to and fro”, but “speaking the truth in love, we must grow up in every way into him who is the head.”

Jesus promises that the one who believes in him will do the works he does, and even greater, and that whatever we ask in his name he will do. St Ambrose, bishop of Milan, lived this: chosen bishop while still a catechumen, he grew into a pastor of great faith who stood firm before emperors and led St Augustine to baptism.
outline: Ask: in what way is your faith still childish?

Prayer in Jesus' name is powerful.
A pastor who grew into greatness and brought Augustine to Christ.

altar: In the Holy Qurbana the whole Body is built up into Christ the Head. Receiving him together, we grow into one mature people.

2026-12-07.question: Where is my faith still childish?

family.explain: Paul tells us to grow strong in faith so that we are not blown around like a leaf in the wind. We grow by prayer, learning and love.
family.intention: We pray for young people in our family, that their faith may grow strong and deep.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us do to learn more about our faith this month?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Head of the Church, you want us to grow to full maturity in you. As we gather, root us in your word and teach us to speak the truth in love. Amen.
share: Paul warns against being tossed by every wind of doctrine (Ephesians 4:14). Which ‘winds’ unsettle my faith today?
How do I speak the truth in love, especially in family arguments?
What step will I take to grow in knowledge of the faith?
interc: For the Church, that she may grow in unity and maturity.
For bishops and teachers of the faith, that like St Ambrose they may speak the truth with courage and love.
For young people confused by many voices, that they may find Christ.
For families divided by arguments, that they may learn to speak the truth in love.
For our parish, that we may grow together into the full stature of Christ.
pm.close: Lord God, you gave St Ambrose wisdom and courage to guide your people. Give us a mature faith, rooted in your Son, so that we may not be shaken but grow in love. Amen.

illus: A coconut seedling planted in loose sand falls over in the first monsoon wind. One planted deep, with good soil around its roots, bends but stands. Our faith needs deep roots before the winds come.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul has a beautiful goal for the Church: that all of us may come to the unity of the faith and the knowledge of the Son of God, to maturity, to the measure of the full stature of Christ (Ephesians 4:13). God wants us to grow up.

Paul describes spiritual childishness: being tossed to and fro and blown about by every wind of doctrine, by people's trickery (Ephesians 4:14). Today the winds blow through our phones: forwarded messages, half-truths, aggressive opinions, new teachings every day. An immature faith is pushed around by every wave.

What is the alternative? Speaking the truth in love, we must grow up in every way into him who is the head, into Christ (Ephesians 4:15). Mature faith is rooted in Christ and the Church's teaching, and it speaks truth always with love: not harsh, not timid.

In the Gospel Jesus promises: whoever believes in me will do the works that I do and, in fact, will do greater works than these; if in my name you ask me for anything, I will do it (John 14:12–14). Asking in Jesus' name means asking as he would ask: for the Father's glory and our true good.

Today we remember St Ambrose, bishop of Milan. He was a mature Christian leader: deeply rooted in Scripture, brave enough to correct the emperor Theodosius after a massacre, gentle enough to welcome his repentance, and wise enough to lead the young Augustine to faith.

How do we grow to maturity? By regular prayer, by knowing the Scriptures, by learning the Catechism, by receiving the sacraments, and by belonging to a community. Faith that is only emotion or only custom stays childish.

This Nombu, let us choose one way to grow: read one chapter of a Gospel each day, join a Bible study, or read the Catechism of the Catholic Church on Christmas. And let us always speak the truth in love. Amen.
kids: Children, St Ambrose helped a young man named Augustine to love Jesus. Pray today for a friend who needs Jesus!

intro: Maturity in faith and confident prayer; St Ambrose.

points.h: Call to me and I will answer
sub: God invites his people to call on him.
Jesus promises to act when we ask in his name.
q: Call to me and I will answer you, and will tell you great and hidden things that you have not known.
I will do whatever you ask in my name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son. If in my name you ask me for anything, I will do it.
points.apply: Bring one intention to Jesus with confidence.

sub: The Church's saints and missionaries prove it.
q: Is anything too wonderful for the LORD?
Very truly, I tell you, the one who believes in me will also do the works that I do and, in fact, will do greater works than these, because I am going to the Father.
points.apply: Do one work of mercy today in Jesus' name.

sub: Mature faith is not tossed about by every teaching.
Ambrose stood firm in truth and love.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; but if you do not, then believe me because of the works themselves.
points.apply: Read one page of the Catechism this week.

concl: Ask in his name, and do his works.
